# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 61 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 61 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_061_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 7 — The Angel of Righteousness and Repentance

**61:1** "I should like to know, lord," I said, "whether those who have died before these days of repentance have any hope for them." "Come," he said, "and I will show you concerning all those who have doubted and have sinned."

**61:2** He showed me a young man sitting in a chair, addressing many people. "Do you see this young man?" he asked. "I see him, lord," I replied. "This is the angel of righteousness," he said. "Standing around him are many people of various kinds. Some are being brought before him; some are going away with joy; and some are going away with grief."

**61:3** "And many," he said, "are standing around listening. Some who come forward to go away are joyful; others grieve and weep." "Lord," I said, "I do not understand what all this means." "Listen," he said. "The young man sitting on the chair is the angel of righteousness. Those who are brought before him are those who are to receive repentance. Hear also why some go away joyful and some sorrowful."

**61:4** "Those who go away joyful are those who have received these words into their hearts and have repented with their whole heart. To them repentance has been given. But those who go away sorrowful are those who have turned completely away from God and do not repent. To these, repentance of life is not given."

**61:5** "But what of those who doubted?" "What of those who have only sinned but not repented?" I asked. "To those who have doubted," he said, "repentance is given in proportion to the disposition of their heart." And he said to me: "Do not give the devil a foothold in your heart. He is crafty and devious in turning aside the servants of God — especially those who are double-minded. So be firm in your faith and do not waver."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and the repentance theology of this transitional chapter.*
